description: Ship extract-shared-types, invert-dependency, and split-file recipes as mechanical executors for known patterns, each validated by the build-green guardrail and released only after history shows ≥10 recurring instances.

requirements.description: Cartographer must ship three refactor recipes as mechanical executors for known conflict patterns: extract-shared-types (AC-RECIPE-EXTRACT-TYPES), invert-dependency (AC-RECIPE-INVERT-DEP), and split-file (AC-RECIPE-SPLIT-FILE). Each recipe must implement a common Recipe interface (AC-RECIPE-INTERFACE) that accepts a Conflict envelope and emits an ordered operation plan. Each recipe must enforce the build-green guardrail (AC-RECIPE-BUILD-GREEN) before reporting success. Recipes must be released only after analytics history shows ≥10 recurring instances of the target pattern.
requirements.title: Refactor Recipes — First Batch of Mechanical Executors

validation.notes: AC-RECIPE-INTERFACE: Recipe interface accepts a Conflict envelope and returns an ordered operation plan without side effects
AC-RECIPE-EXTRACT-TYPES: Given a type-only cycle conflict, recipe emits operations to move shared types to a new shared package
AC-RECIPE-INVERT-DEP: Given a cross-domain cycle conflict, recipe emits operations to introduce an interface and invert the dependency direction
AC-RECIPE-SPLIT-FILE: Given a junk-drawer conflict, recipe emits operations to split the file by domain responsibility
AC-RECIPE-BUILD-GREEN: Recipe executor refuses to report success if build is broken after applying its operations
extract-shared-types recipe applied to bas/fixtures/go-cycles/ resolves the type-only cycle and build remains green
invert-dependency recipe applied to a fixture cross-domain cycle resolves the conflict and build remains green
split-file recipe applied to bas/fixtures/ts-junk-drawer/ reduces junk-drawer node degree and build remains green
Analytics records recipe execution event after each successful recipe application
Each recipe is only available in production after ≥10 analytics-confirmed recurring instances of its target pattern
A recipe never makes a business-logic decision; it only performs mechanical structural transformations

title: Refactor Recipes (First Batch)
